# Bearing-Noise Sensitivity Study — Results

**Problem ID:** DRDO DIA-CoE/EW/02
**Generated by:** `bearing_noise_study.py` (seed 42, N=2 realizations/cell, 344 s trial time)
**Inputs:** `data/processed/test_signals.csv` — 72 ground-truth signals (8 azimuths × {800, 1500, 2200} km × 3 conditions, AH223 receiver, 2012-06-15)
**Per-trial data:** `data/processed/bearing_noise_results.csv` (2,304 trials = 72 signals × 16 cells × 2)

> **Revision (D8, 2026-07-11):** regenerated after the D8 fix — PyRayHF now
> ray-traces at the request frequency with the corrected vertical
> group-refractive-index integral (the earlier per-layer `find_vh` misuse is
> fixed). Storm-condition signals are synthesized at 10 MHz through the
> corrected physics; six of the 24 storm-condition emitter geometries
> penetrate at 10 MHz and fall back to IRI heights. Figures below supersede
> the 2026-07-11 pre-D8 tables.

Each cell aggregates 144 trials (two Gaussian draws per signal). The latency
probe measured ~0.11 s per real ionosphere call and sized N=2; 1,525 real
model calls served 4,608 memoised lookups.

## Interpretation

- **Intrinsic floor (0, 0):** median **4.2 km**, P90 92.3 km, MAE 48.3 km —
  the algorithm's own error with perfect bearings (two-pass midpoint
  refinement + spherical-geometry approximation only). The mean sits above
  the median because the storm-condition signals remain heavy-tailed: the
  corrected 10 MHz ray-traced heights vary strongly with position, and the
  pass-one receiver height mislocates the bounce midpoint, amplified by
  1/tan(Δ) at longer ranges. The corrected physics also raises the true
  elevations (7°–43° versus 3°–22° pre-D8), which softens the low-elevation
  amplification relative to the earlier study.
- **Elevation error dominates:** at equal σ it costs ~3× more than azimuth
  error (median 143.2 km for 2.0° elevation noise alone versus 43.0 km for
  2.0° azimuth noise alone; 67.4 versus 27.3 km at 1.0°). Elevation enters
  through d = hᵥ/tan(Δ), so elevation error converts directly into range
  error.
- **Azimuth error mainly rotates the fix:** az-only medians grow gently
  (4.2 → 14.4 → 27.3 → 43.0 km), consistent with cross-range displacement of
  approximately range × sin σ.
- **Sampling caveat:** with two draws per signal per cell, cell aggregates
  rest on 144 trials; the MAE columns are not perfectly monotone (heavy
  tails dominate means). The medians are monotone in both axes.

## Scope and honesty

- Single-hop, mid-latitude India geometry only (receiver AH223, 23.0°N 72.6°E).
- **Same-model isolation:** observations are synthesized and inverted with the
  same hybrid ionosphere, so ionospheric *model* error is excluded by design —
  it is characterized separately in `docs/results.md`. The numbers here
  measure the SSL algorithm itself under bearing error.
- Elevation noise is clipped to the solver's validated 1°–60° band.
- Memoised ionosphere lookups quantized to 0.1° (~11 km); deterministic
  (seed 42, fixed loop order).
